findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" has no || exit guard, unlike every sibling script this repo's own convention requires (build-artifacts.sh:22, add-regression-case.sh:21, run-regression-set.sh:20). If git rev-parse --show-toplevel fails, ROOT becomes an empty string; SCRIPTS and PACKS then resolve to wrong absolute paths, the subsequent cp of the real scripts into the throwaway repo silently fails, and the test proceeds to build-artifacts.sh calls that never actually run the intended script, cascading into the D1 assertion's blind-pass bug below instead of a clear, early error.
evidence: tests/run-integration.sh:6 — ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" with no || { echo ...; exit N; }
tests/run-integration.sh:7-8 — SCRIPTS="$ROOT/...", PACKS="$ROOT/..." built directly off the unguarded ROOT
tests/run-integration.sh:20 — cp "$SCRIPTS/build-artifacts.sh" "$SCRIPTS/validate-pack.sh" ... fails silently if ROOT was empty, with nothing checking its exit status

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: The D1 assertion is inverted relative to D3's: an if that treats grep failing to match — for any reason, including $OUT being empty/wrong or wiring.txt not existing at all — the same as a genuinely clean pass. A broken pipeline run reads as "ok D1: wiring.txt clean" instead of failing loudly, unlike the D3 check just below it which uses a non-inverted grep and correctly falls through to its FAIL branch on the same kind of missing-file case.
evidence: tests/run-integration.sh:30-31 — OUT="$(... | grep '^OUT=' | cut -d= -f2)", empty if build-artifacts.sh never printed that line
tests/run-integration.sh:32 — if grep -qE '\$\(|echo' "$OUT/wiring.txt" 2>/dev/null; then — no-match (including missing/empty file) falls to else
tests/run-integration.sh:36 — else branch prints "ok   D1: wiring.txt clean" even when nothing was actually checked
tests/run-integration.sh:43-47 — the D3 check right below uses the same shape without inversion and correctly FAILs on a missing/empty run.env

findings.label: contract
findings.failure_mode: This diff's D3 fix makes build-artifacts.sh write a new file, $OUT/brief-probes-stderr, whenever the domain pack's Brief probes block errors at runtime. The script's own header comment block, which this repo's contract convention requires document the script's interface, still lists only the pre-existing artifact set and was not updated, so a caller/tooling author reading the documented interface to know what's in $OUT has no way to learn this file exists.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:14 — header lists only patch.diff manifest.txt brief.txt wiring.txt (no mention of brief-probes-stderr)
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:376 — ( eval "$PROBES"; ... ) 2>"$OUT/brief-probes-stderr" newly writes that file into $OUT
.claude/skills/pr-review/SKILL.md:46 — the same diff's own $OUT artifact table also has no row for brief-probes-stderr, so neither doc surface reflects the new file

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: A domain pack missing/renaming one of the 5 required headings trips two independently hand-typed copies of the same heading-check loop with different severities: build-artifacts.sh's own inline check only warns and never gates, while the new call into validate-pack.sh's separate copy of the same check fails and is now wired into STALE=1 by this diff, which empties every probes-*.txt and the Dependencies block for the whole pack instead of just the one affected section, contradicting this same file's/SKILL.md's own documented single-section degrade.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:52 — for h in the five heading strings / grep -qxF "$h" "$PACK" || MISSING_HEADINGS=... (warns only, never sets STALE)
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:18 — grep -qxF "$h" "$PACK" || fail "missing or renamed heading: $h" (independent hand-typed second copy of the same check)

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:76-79 — bash "$VALIDATOR" "$PACK"; if [ $? = 1 ]; then PACK_INVALID=1; STALE=1 (new: wires the duplicate check's failure into the shared STALE gate)

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:400 — if [ "$PACK_PRESENT" = 1 ] && [ "$STALE" = 0 ] (gates ALL label probes/Dependencies on STALE, so the second copy's harsher verdict on the same condition empties everything, not just the one section)
